title: Black-background effect luminance to alpha (core nodes, draft)
summary: Black-background glow/spark/smoke still -> RGBA PNG; alpha = 1-(1-R)(1-G)(1-B). Core nodes only, no model.
status_note: Draft. The same graph ran once by direct HTTP on windows-cuda (2026-11-05, one synthetic effect, about 0.5 s); not yet run through this runner. Colour is not un-premultiplied and there is no black point / gamma, so straight-alpha compositing looks darker than the local vfx luma-alpha script. Single image only; video untested.

provenance.derived_from: docs/experiments/2026-11-05-bg-removal/luma_alpha_core.api.json; only LoadImage.image replaced by the __IMAGE__ placeholder.

upstream.note: Built for this repo from core nodes (ImageToMask, InvertMask, MaskComposite multiply, JoinImageWithAlpha). No official workflow template or blueprint does luminance-to-alpha.

evidence.note: 2026-11-05 Windows RTX 4080: MAE 0.074 straight / 0.046 premultiplied vs BiRefNet 0.088 and vfx luma-alpha 0.029
When to use which background-removal method

image.help: 純黑底的特效靜圖（發光、火花、亮色煙）。不是黑底的圖不要用。

fixed_notes: alpha = 1-(1-R)(1-G)(1-B); RGB kept as is (premultiplied-looking). Black pixels become fully transparent, so dark or opaque smoke loses body. No model download.
